findings.fixArea: WAL-reset database-corruption race fixed in 3.51.3 and later
findings.assessment: The workload uses WAL and multiple processes, so this historical bug class is directly relevant. Both tested runtimes are newer than 3.51.3 and therefore include the documented fix.

findings.fixArea: database mutex coverage for busy-timeout, autocommit/error/change-count/last-rowid and related APIs
findings.assessment: The adapters use synchronous JavaScript calls and never share one connection across workers; each process owns a separate connection. The additional 3.53.3 mutex hardening is still desirable defense in depth.

findings.fixArea: backup crash when deserialize occurs after backup initialization
findings.assessment: Neither adapter exposes or calls deserialize.

findings.fixArea: backup use-after-free associated with ATTACH during active backup
findings.assessment: ATTACH is absent from the static SQL surface; node:sqlite additionally denies it through an authorizer, and neither wrapper exposes raw SQL.

findings.fixArea: WAL/SHM corrupt-header, huge-map, and Windows long-path hardening
findings.assessment: The qualification used Linux, ordinary paths, small WALs, and databases created by the same adapter. These fixes matter for hostile or corrupted inputs but were not exercised by the normal workload.
Useful to fail closed on damaged files, but the synthetic restart and backup databases remained well formed and passed quick_check.

findings.fixArea: row-value IN, COLLATE, REAL/INT UPSERT, JSON/window, FTS, session, and extension fixes
findings.assessment: The fixed query shapes and optional modules are outside the closed schema and SQL used here.

conclusion: Both runtimes include the directly relevant WAL-reset fix, but neither contains the complete 3.53.3 maintenance set. The missing fixes do not map to an exercised normal path in this closed workload, yet a production decision should wait for or separately qualify a runtime carrying source ID d4c0e51e... or later.
